title: Food's Revenge
text: “Heroes?”
“Ah, sorry. So, which regions are activated right now, again?”
The Queen, who had been standing outside the conversation, continued to speak, I say.

“Yes… this concerns both an apology for the recent incident and an arrangement for strengthening the heroes… though having witnessed the battle in question, I cannot rule out the possibility that such strengthening may prove unnecessary.”
“It’s fine. We’ll gratefully accept the opportunity to participate.”
“What a bother. But I’ll go.”
Here Rafumi, still disguised as Ren, wore a smile as if to say she too intended to participate.
“Fostering exchange among the heroes and cooperation between companions is also part of the plan, though… it seems exchange has already taken place.”
“That’s right. There’s already exchange with Ren’s party and Itsuki’s party, so it should be unnecessary. Motoyasu-kun and I are practically the same anyway.”
“Yeah, the people my country arranged for me have wandered off somewhere. I suppose Rishia-san and the like count as my companions now?”
Itsuki, having sold off his own companions, dropped that bombshell, I say.
“I wonder if Émia will come?”

“She’s not one to indulge in luxury much… still, using the activated region to thoroughly strengthen her might indeed be a good idea. It’d raise the odds of fending off any strange intruders while I’m away, and a southern country might set a pleasant mood too.”
Public order in Melromarc was apparently quite bad. Something about a fundamental shortage of soldiers. So there was value in making everyone strong, partly as a form of self-defense, I say.
“Cal Mira Island might be good for Itsuki’s care too.”

“I don’t care about myself, really. Should we pair the rabbit guy with Rishia-san too, Naofumi-san? Let’s gather the Rumo-species folk and strengthen them as well. Rumo-species are great—very mogu-mogu.”
“Itsuki… you really have changed. You’re a lot like Motoyasu-kun now.”
“That’s outrageous. Please don’t lump Filolials and Rumo-species together. They’re very skillful, gentle people, you know?”
“Do you wish to die, Itsuki!”
“Hmph. I’m just stating facts. The Rumo-species are docile, aren’t they?”
“Vof… depending on the region, there are bandit Rumo-species in Siltvelt who ravage farmland.”
Wolf fired off some covering fire on my behalf, I say. See, look at that!
“Now, now… not every member of a race is good, Itsuki. Affirming that kind of thing wholesale makes you just like Motoyasu-kun.”
“Ngh… fine, I understand. But it’s still true that most Rumo-species in this country are good people.”
“Well, sure. Then having them get a bit stronger on Cal Mira Island might be good too.”
It seemed the conversation was heading toward actually going.
“Vof, southern country date.”
“That’s something I cannot let slide, is it not?”
“One does call it a date.”
Somehow Wolf, Crocodile Guy, and Rabbit Guy had begun glaring at each other, I say.
“Personally I’d like to prioritize reconstruction… but perhaps I should prioritize strengthening instead?”
Éclair was troubled, I say.
“No need to worry, Éclair. Reconstruction would go faster with Elephant in charge of command than with Éclair handling it, I say.”
“Eclair-sama, I don’t think you should take that too much to heart.”
“But… Shion, you want to go, don’t you?”
“Wolf and the others are saying things I cannot let slide, so I dare not take my eyes off them…”
“Vof, Shion can go help with reconstruction, is fine.”
“That’s right. Leave the rest to us.”
“No, it’s simply a fact that it’s better to entrust things to Elmelo-dono than to leave them to Eclair-sama.”
“Shion.”
“Mm…”
Éclair, looking somewhat displeased, closed her eyes and scolded Crocodile Guy. Elephant was quite capable, I say.
“Somehow it seems like it’s already been decided that Elmelo-san will be left in charge while we’re away.”
“Eh, Elmelo’s not coming? Should Kou stop going too?”
Kou liked playing with Elephant, after all.
“Er… I’d be grateful if you could tell me the number of people coming beforehand.”
“Sounds like there might be a headcount limit with how this is going. Let’s all discuss that a bit.”
“Thank you kindly, Heroes.”
“If sleeping on the beach outdoors is fine, Gaelion could carry everyone there on her back, nano.”
“That’s something to discuss too.”
And so… once the banquet ended and night deepened, everyone dispersed and headed home, I say.

This happened after that banquet had ended, I say. Rival called out to Father, me, and Rafumi, and we ended up having a secret talk in a room. We gathered after putting Yuki-chan and the others to bed.
“Gaelion-chan. What’s this about?”
“It’s about the bitch ex-princess thing from earlier today, nano.”
“…Sounds like you’ve got some idea who’s behind it. You told Motoyasu-kun to keep quiet about it, and it seems like you gathered us like this so no one would overhear.”
“Nano.”
With that, Rival turned to face Rafumi, who was still disguised as Ren.
“Confess already, nano.”
“You speak of confessing as though there’s something to confess. Do you have proof that I’m the culprit?”

“No proof, nano. But it’s clear the Spear Hero isn’t the culprit—he’s scheming to make the bastard suffer far worse—and Gaelion isn’t the culprit either, so anyone can see that leaves you as the culprit, nano.”
“What did you say!? You went and did it, damn you!”
I had wanted to make the Crimson Swine suffer even more, and yet someone had gone and done it first!
“Fu!”
Rafumi scoffed through her nose, I say. How dare she finish off the Crimson Swine by such an easy method!
“I was planning to make it suffer far more, I say.”
“Ugh… what an awful thing to say. The idea that dying here was actually a mercy, and you’re complaining about that…”

Father’s merciful words were wasted on the Crimson Swine, I say. The crime of killing Fleon-chan ran that deep. What’s more, being an apostle of Ouroboros meant its very soul had been altered, making it impossible to salvage the soul afterward for torture or anything else, I say.
“By process of elimination… can you truly deny the possibility that, through some twist of fate, it happened to restock its own deadly poison?”

“Even if that were somehow possible, its belongings should have been checked during transport, nano. In the first place, it only learned who it intended to poison this very morning, so the timing wouldn’t add up, nano.”
“Fine, have it your way. Indeed, I am the culprit.”
“So it was you after all!”
“Yes. Well, there are various reasons, but as a spirit, my reasoning was that exceeding the bounds of a hero’s dignity in retaliation—going beyond all limits—simply will not do.”
“Like I care about any of that, I say!”
The Crimson Swine was going to properly receive its due punishment, I say.
“Don’t say that. I too believe it’s bad to let this become habitual—that’s one reason. Surely you understand that much, don’t you?”
“You’re the one who did it, nano.”
“There’s a bit of a difference forming here, isn’t there? This time, I am the culprit.”
Rival sighed at this, I say. What exactly had she come to understand?
“So, what’s the second reason, nano?”
“The second reason is that I wished to utterly annihilate anyone who mixes poison into food and feeds it to someone. Surely you know what kind of spirit I originally was?”
Rafumi had originally been a chocolate monster, I say.
“I wanted to make it receive the same punishment—poisoning its food in kind.”
“I won’t deny that it—or rather, those connected to it—often use that very trick, nano. But I don’t think you should be doing it either, nano.”
“Consider it food’s revenge.”
“I always wonder—just what perspective is Rafumi-chan even speaking from?”
“Sometimes food, sometimes a spirit, sometimes an artificial life form—that is… me!”
And with that, Rafumi struck some kind of pose that looked exactly like something an awakened Ren would do, I say.
“So… how exactly did you poison it, nano?”
Rival asked, sounding rather put out, I say. Damn you, Rafumi, I say.

“Hmph. There are plenty of ways to avoid suspicion. One method would have been to hide alongside the poison already in the dish it stole from the kitchen in a past loop, when it tried to poison the Shield Hero—concealing my poison within its own. But what I actually used this time was… I swapped the contents of the poison vial it had procured. After that, it destroyed itself all on its own.”
“Well, aren’t you something, managing a swap like that, nano. What about the one in its room?”
“That one—whether it knew or not—I refilled just to be safe.”
So that’s why the contents had actually been there!? I was left speechless at just how far Rafumi’s covert scheming had reached.
